prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH) and at least 40% value addition (VA). CTSH means each non-originating input must be classified in a different 6-digit subheading than the product. VA is the share of the product's price that does not come from non-originating materials. The product cannot be checked yet because no checks have been run, as the 6-digit HS code for the emollients input is missing.

notes.text: '+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Estimate is on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
